title: I Let the Cat-Cafe Visit Timer Catch the Regular Who Camped the Window

parts.text: I checked in at 11:08 a.m. for a sixty-minute visit and seat W1 was still occupied by regular Nora with a laptop. The chalkboard said: ONE HOUR. LAPTOPS AFTER THE CAT NAP. Nora did not move. I was twenty-three, walk-in, holding a timer chit. "Regulars are naps." I photographed the chalkboard, the chit, and her power brick in the cat tree. Then I logged a camp. At 11:16 the owner asked why Nora's brick was on a visit-overtime ticket. I let them finish the sentence they would regret in writing. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see Nora's power brick on the cat tree against the one-hour chalkboard.

social.video_title: She camped the window seat past the visit timer — Part 1/2
social.description: Cat cafe, a laptop, and a chalkboard hour she ignores. I logged the camp. Would you have waited with the chit?

parts.text: Nora called it bonding until the owner asked for the ticket. I printed the camp, the photo, and the chit. W1 opened. Nora bonded from the laptop bench and told the line naps were always about optics. Optics is a word regulars use when a brick exists. Visit policy now has a second line: REGULARS ARE NOT THE WINDOW. I keep my hour. Nora unplugs. The cafe finally looks like cats, not a coworking. Nobody thanked me, which is how you know a policy finally works. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.

social.description: Camp ticket, open seat, and a second line. Was bonding ever a power brick?
